_meta.description: Which loot tables retail hung on each floor-item spawn point.
_meta.why: generate_for_dungeon takes a spawn's tables from its interactable in parsed.json. Retail named at least one table that mapping does not on 0 of the 0 spawns seen here. Mostly town resources -- but one of them is 8858f284-4f33-4da4-8085-0befa7ef2637, a 100% DoorKey table that retail hung on three of the sixty pots in The Wizard's Challenge, so the key never dropped and the locked door could not open (#192).
_meta.shape: the table set is a property of the SPAWN POINT: of the 969 spawns observed more than once, 948 always carried the same set and 21 varied. `tables` is the modal set; `distribution` keeps the rest.
_meta.unobservedSpawns: a spawn absent from this file keeps the current behaviour -- the consumer falls back to the interactable's own tables and must not invent one.
_meta.consumer: blades_lib/src/util/dungeon.rs: spawn_loot_tables() unions this with the interactable's tables. Union rather than replace because the gap is one-directional (0 spawns gain a table, 0 would lose one).
_meta.deduplication: on (questId, sha1 of the dungeon entry), same as the other corpora
